title: Contrastive Text-enhanced Transformer for Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Cross-domain sequential recommendation seeks to improve recommendation in a target domain by using users' sequential preferences from a source domain.

gap.claim: Existing approaches struggle with sparse data and, in text-based methods, face challenges in modeling shared semantic relationships, integrating semantic and behavioral intents, and providing sufficient supervision.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes CTT, a text-enhanced cross-domain sequential recommendation solution that jointly learns semantic and behavioral user preferences.
CTT uses inter-domain and intra-domain preference views, including domain-shared cross-attention, semantic and behavioral intent extraction, and preference integration for next-item prediction.
CTT introduces semantic-behavior contrastive learning to enhance cross-domain preference learning and knowledge transfer.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CTT as a novel text-enhanced cross-domain sequential recommendation solution.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On three real-world datasets, the authors report that CTT outperforms state-of-the-art models by an average of 5.86% on HR@5.
The authors report that preprocessing scripts, experiment configurations, source code, and baseline implementations are available in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: CDSR transfers sequential preferences from a source domain to improve recommendation in a target domain.
Neural sequence models face sparse data, while text-based methods face semantic-sharing, intent-integration, and supervision challenges.
CTT jointly models semantic and behavioral preferences through inter-domain and intra-domain views with attention and intent extraction.
Semantic-behavior contrastive learning is added to improve cross-domain preference learning and knowledge transfer.
The authors report improved HR@5 results on three datasets and release implementation materials.

source_observation.claim: The method combines semantic and behavioral preferences using separate inter-domain and intra-domain views.

interpretation.claim: Separating cross-domain semantic transfer from within-domain preference modeling may help organize heterogeneous signals.

application.claim: For cross-domain sequential recommendation, consider distinct modules for shared semantic relations and domain-specific behavioral patterns before integrating them.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation helps across domains or datasets beyond the reported experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three datasets, baselines, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide ablations, statistical uncertainty, or details of the model architecture and training procedure.
